claims.text: A molybdenum interlayer can be introduced between tungsten and CuCrZr.
Introducing a molybdenum interlayer will improve the integrity of a tungsten/CuCrZr joint.
Introducing a molybdenum interlayer will reduce thermal stresses in a tungsten/CuCrZr joint during fusion-reactor operation.
The initial material state is a directly joined tungsten/CuCrZr assembly without an intermediate layer.
A thin molybdenum layer is deposited and integrated between tungsten and CuCrZr during fabrication.
Fusion-reactor divertor conditions involve high thermal loads and cyclic temperature variations.
Molybdenum has thermal-expansion properties intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has mechanical properties intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum's coefficient of thermal expansion is closer to those of both tungsten and CuCrZr.
The thermal-expansion characteristics of molybdenum will reduce residual thermal stresses at the tungsten/CuCrZr interface.
Molybdenum has a high melting point.
Molybdenum's high melting point and high-temperature stability help maintain a robust mechanical bond under cyclic loading.
Molybdenum-containing interlayers will reduce crack formation during thermal cycling compared with direct tungsten/CuCrZr joints.
Molybdenum-containing interlayers will improve interfacial bonding strength during thermal cycling compared with direct tungsten/CuCrZr joints.
Direct tungsten/CuCrZr interfaces are prone to high residual stresses.
High residual stresses in direct tungsten/CuCrZr interfaces can cause delamination or cracking under cyclic thermal loads.
The effect of the molybdenum interlayer may vary under different thermal or mechanical loading regimes.
